composition: This sample belongs to the Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C-0.04Nb (wt%) medium-Mn low-density steel family. Its measured strip composition is 12.82 Mn, 9.12 Al, 2.99 Cr, 1.40 C, 0.039 Nb with Fe balance (wt%), essentially identical to the 0.02Nb counterpart except for the roughly doubled Nb content (0.039 vs 0.021 wt%). Fe is the matrix element; Mn and Al are the principal alloying additions that stabilize austenite and reduce density, respectively, while the high C level supports κ-carbide formation and Cr is added at about 3 wt%. The deliberate microalloying addition of 0.039 wt% Nb is intended to form NbC and regulate the microstructure and κ-carbide precipitation. EPMA-measured austenite composition is 13.03 Mn, 8.37 Al, 3.97 Cr, 1.33 C, 0.038 Nb, 64.07 Fe (wt%); Nb is essentially uniformly dissolved in the austenite grain interior with only sporadic grain-boundary enrichment, so the κ-carbide-forming elements Al and C in austenite remain essentially unchanged relative to the 0.02Nb steel.
conclusions: The 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h demonstrates that 0.04 wt% Nb microalloying in Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C low-density steel refines the austenite grain (≈9 μm) through NbC pinning while suppressing κ-carbide coarsening via an elevated κ-carbide formation energy and reduced C diffusivity. Its duplex ferrite + austenite phase constitution (18.4 vol% ferrite) is unaffected by the aging treatment, which instead promotes NbC and κ-carbide growth without forming coarsened intergranular κ-carbides. At 773 K/3 h, κ-carbide precipitation is the principal strengthening factor (156.8 MPa in austenite), giving a yield strength of 1014 ± 16 MPa, tensile strength of 1122 ± 14 MPa, elongation of 14 ± 2 % and hardness of 465 HV. Relative to the 0.02Nb steel at the same condition, it shows higher yield strength (1014 vs 975 MPa) but lower ductility (14 vs 17 % elongation), illustrating the strength–ductility trade-off in this aging series and the value of Nb microalloying for tailoring nano-precipitation and strength in medium-Mn low-density steels.

identity.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h

mechanisms: NbC grain-boundary pinning refines the austenite grain: because Nb strongly raises the MC (NbC) precipitation temperature (from ≈973 to 1573 K as Nb increases from 0 to 0.05 wt%), submicron NbC particles form at high temperature and pin austenite grain boundaries during the δ→γ transformation, halving the austenite grain size of the 0.04Nb steel (≈9 μm) relative to the 0.02Nb steel (≈18 μm) and thereby raising Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening (≈125.8 MPa vs ≈89.9 MPa at 773 K).

Nb doping destabilizes κ-carbide: DFT calculations show that doping Nb into κ-carbide raises its formation energy from 0.891 eV (Fe24Al8C8) to 2.826 eV (Fe23NbAl8C8, Nb on the Fe site) or 1.453 eV (Fe24Al7NbC8, Nb on the Al site), so Nb atoms incorporated in κ-carbide make it less stable and suppress κ-carbide nucleation and growth, explaining why the 0.04Nb steel always contains smaller and fewer κ-carbides than the 0.02Nb steel.

Nb slows C diffusion and thus decelerates κ growth: Thermo-Calc diffusion calculations (673–873 K) show that Nb slightly lowers the C diffusion coefficient in austenite owing to strong Nb–C affinity while slightly raising Al diffusivity; since κ-carbide growth and coarsening are governed mainly by C diffusion, this slower C transport further retards κ-carbide nucleation and growth in the 0.04Nb steel.

Aging trades dislocation strengthening for precipitation strengthening: at 773 K/3 h the austenite dislocation density falls to 1.03 × 10^14 m^-2 (dislocation strengthening 106.1 MPa versus 169.8 MPa as-cast), while growth of nano-scale κ-carbides raises their precipitation strengthening to 156.8 MPa, the dominant austenite contribution, yielding a net yield strength of 1014 MPa with reduced ductility (14 %).

Nb produces a net strength gain through competing mechanisms: relative to the 0.02Nb steel, the 0.04Nb steel gains additional dislocation strengthening and grain-boundary strengthening but loses some κ-carbide precipitation strengthening (fewer and smaller κ-carbides); the net effect is a higher overall yield strength for the 0.04Nb steel (≈71 MPa above the 0.02Nb steel on average) but poorer plasticity.
microstructure: This sample exhibits a duplex ferrite + austenite microstructure. Irregular-shaped δ-ferrite (bcc) islands are randomly dispersed within the austenite (fcc) matrix, with ferrite content measured at 18.4 vol% and austenite comprising the remaining >80 vol% as the matrix. The austenite grain size is about 9 μm and the ferrite grain size about 3.1 μm (as-cast values; the austenite grain size remains almost unchanged after aging). Submicron NbC particles are dispersed within the austenite matrix, and dense nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides (Fe3AlC, E21 ordered) are present, coherent with austenite with a cube-on-cube [100]γ // [100]κ orientation relationship. XRD shows only ferrite and austenite reflections, with no new phase after aging; the 773 K/3 h treatment does not measurably change the phase constitution but promotes NbC and κ-carbide growth, and no coarsened intergranular κ-carbides are observed. From XRD line-profile analysis, the austenite dislocation density is 1.03 × 10^14 m^-2 with microstrain 0.07, while the ferrite dislocation density is 1.10 × 10^15 m^-2 with microstrain 0.257. Relative to the 0.02Nb steel, this 0.04Nb steel consistently contains smaller and fewer intragranular κ-carbides.
processing: The steel was prepared by centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification: an ingot was first induction-melted in a water-cooled copper crucible, then re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold to obtain steel strips of 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm. A portion of the as-cast strip was subsequently aged in a tubular vacuum furnace at 773 K for 3 h. The 773 K/3 h condition belongs to the study's 723–823 K, 3 h aging-temperature series applied to the near-rapidly solidified as-cast material; no cold or hot rolling is reported for this sample.
properties: Tensile testing (ambient temperature, strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1, gauge width 4 mm and gauge length 12 mm, MTS Criterion 44) gives a yield strength of 1014 ± 16 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1122 ± 14 MPa and a total elongation of 14 ± 2 %. Vickers microhardness (indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s) is 465 HV. Characterization included XRD (D/max-2500, 40 kV, 30°–100°, 4°/min) for phase identification and line-profile analysis; SEM with EBSD (step size 300 nm) for morphology and ferrite content (ImageJ); TEM (JEOL JEM-2100, 200 kV) with dark-field imaging, SAED and EDS for NbC and κ-carbide identification; EPMA for elemental distribution; and Thermo-Calc (TCFE10 and TCFE10_MOBFE5 databases) plus VASP spin-polarized DFT for thermodynamic, diffusion and formation-energy calculations. Quantitative strengthening analysis attributes austenite contributions at this condition of 106.1 MPa (dislocation), 125.8 MPa (grain boundary), 156.8 MPa (κ-carbide precipitation) and 4.6 MPa (NbC Orowan), with ferrite dislocation strengthening of approximately 96.4 MPa.
summary: The 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h is a Nb-microalloyed Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C (wt%) medium-Mn low-density steel strip produced by near-rapid solidification and then aged in vacuum. It is one aging state within a study of how 0.04 wt% Nb regulates the nano-precipitation (submicron NbC and nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides) and the resulting mechanical properties of medium-Mn low-density steel.
